title: Dental-Care Benefits
subtitle: Confirm coverage and price before the chair begins reclining

blocks.text: A dental chair is no place to discover that “covered” and “free” are distant cousins who only exchange holiday cards.

The Canadian Dental Care Plan, or CDCP, helps Canadian residents who cannot get private dental coverage and whose adjusted family net income is below $90,000. It pays dental providers who take part, using CDCP rules and set fees. You may still owe a co-payment, the gap between the clinic’s price and the plan’s fee, or the full cost of a service the plan does not cover.
All four rules matter: no access to private dental insurance, your Canadian tax returns filed, adjusted family net income below $90,000 and living in Canada.

items.title: “Declining available workplace dental insurance makes me eligible for CDCP.”
items.text: If you can get private coverage, you may not qualify, even if you choose not to sign up or pay for it. The plan checks access, not enthusiasm.

blocks.text: Canada: CDCP eligibility
Knowing what “covered” means before treatment protects you from a dental bill you did not plan for.
blocks.detail: Your income band, the plan’s set fee and the clinic’s price together decide what you pay.
blocks.extra: Section 02 shows how your income band sets your share.

sections.title: Coverage Has Dates, Percentages and Rules

blocks.text: Once approved, you get a coverage start date and information from Service Canada and Sun Life. Do not book treatment before your coverage starts. CDCP does not pay you back if you pay the whole bill yourself. The clinic sends claims straight to the plan.

items.title: AFNI BELOW $70,000
items.text: CDCP pays 100% of the set fee for covered services. The clinic may still charge you more.

items.title: AFNI $70,000 TO $79,999
items.text: CDCP pays 60% of the set fee and you pay 40%, plus any extra the clinic charges.

items.title: AFNI $80,000 TO $89,999
items.text: CDCP pays 40% of the set fee and you pay 60%, plus any extra the clinic charges.

items.title: AFNI $90,000 OR MORE
items.text: You do not meet the income rule for that benefit period.

blocks.text: A clinic’s usual price may be higher than the CDCP set fee. Before treatment, ask whether the clinic will charge you the difference, often called balance billing.
CDCP can work alongside some provincial, territorial and federal dental programs. The rules vary, so show every coverage letter to your clinic.

items.title: “A 0% co-payment means the appointment must cost the member nothing.”
items.text: Zero percent applies to covered CDCP services at the set fee. Services the plan does not cover, and clinic prices above the CDCP amount, can still create a bill.

blocks.text: Canada: CDCP coverage

sections.title: Ask Four Questions Before You Say Yes

blocks.text: Get the estimate before the chair reclines, not after.

items.title: Is this service covered by CDCP?
items.text: Ask for the service code and check whether you have already used up the number of times it is allowed.

items.title: Is preauthorization needed?
items.text: Some services need the plan to review them first. Wait for that answer before you book.

items.title: What will CDCP pay?
items.text: Ask for the plan’s set fee and the share CDCP pays for your income band.

items.title: What will I owe in total?
items.text: Add your co-payment to any difference between the clinic’s price and the set fee. Ask for that total in writing.

blocks.text: Preauthorization is a coverage review. It is not permission for treatment, and it does not promise that every future charge will be paid. The clinic sends it in with the papers needed.
Limits on how often matter. A service can be in the benefits guide and still not be covered, because you have already used the allowed number or timing.

items.title: “If a dentist recommends a service, CDCP must cover it.”
items.text: A dentist’s advice and what the plan covers answer different questions. You and your dentist decide on care. The plan applies its coverage rules.

blocks.text: Key takeaway: CDCP is not a blank cheque. Check your coverage date, the service code, any preauthorization, the set fee, your co-payment and the clinic’s price difference before treatment starts.

sections.title: Renée and the Crown With Two Prices

blocks.text: Meet Renée
paragraphs: Renée Gagnon lives in Moncton and has CDCP coverage. A cracked back tooth needs a crown, and her goal is to get it fixed before it breaks. The clinic says the crown is “covered,” a word Renée’s budget hears as “please leave your wallet in the car.”
The front desk is ready to book her for Thursday. Renée is ready too. The tooth hurts.
Then she remembers a line from her CDCP letter: her family income puts her in the 40% co-payment band. She asks a simple question. How much will I pay, in dollars?

The receptionist does not know. The crown needs preauthorization first, and the clinic’s price is higher than the CDCP set fee. Renée has a choice. She can book Thursday and sort out the bill later, or wait for a written estimate. She chooses to wait.
Two weeks later, the clinic gives her a breakdown: what CDCP will pay, her 40% share and the $180 gap between the clinic’s price and the set fee. Her total is $640.

That is more than Renée can pay at once. Her dentist suggests another option the plan also covers, and the clinic offers to split her share over three months. Renée picks the crown and the payment plan.
The crown does not become cheap by vocabulary. It becomes understandable, which is the useful first step between a treatment plan and a payment plan.

blocks.text: Never rely on a percentage someone says out loud. Ask for the service codes and your estimate, so you and the clinic are talking about the same service, tooth and fee.
What resolved the conflict?
“Covered” is a coverage category, not a price. Check the codes, the preauthorization and the fee breakdown in writing before you agree to treatment.
Renée turned a vague “covered” into a $640 total she could plan for by waiting for a written estimate.
blocks.detail: Asking for the dollar amount in writing protects your own budget before any treatment starts.
blocks.extra: The quick check in Section 05 tests whether you can spot the next move.

items.title: What four rules make up the CDCP eligibility check?
items.detail: No access to private dental insurance, Canadian tax returns filed, adjusted family net income below $90,000 and living in Canada.

items.title: Why might you still owe money with a 0% co-payment?
items.detail: Zero percent applies to covered CDCP services at the set fee. Services the plan does not cover, and clinic prices above the CDCP amount, can still create a bill.

items.title: Who sends a CDCP claim?
items.detail: The clinic sends covered claims straight to the plan. CDCP does not pay you back if you pay the full bill yourself.

items.title: What does preauthorization decide, and what does it not decide?
items.detail: It is a coverage review done before some treatments. It is not permission for treatment, and it does not promise that every future charge will be paid.

items.title: Why tell your clinic about every other dental plan you have?
items.detail: CDCP can work alongside some provincial, territorial and federal dental programs, and the rules vary, so your clinic needs every coverage letter.

sections.title: Your Action (Fill Out Form): Dental Coverage and Cost Confirmation Sheet

blocks.text: Do not write member numbers, health card numbers or full dental records. Keep the official letters and estimates somewhere safe.
You must renew CDCP coverage every year. Missing the renewal window can leave a gap, and services you get during the gap are not paid back later.

items.title: Established fee
items.text: The amount CDCP uses to work out what it pays.

items.title: Co-payment
items.text: Your share, as a percentage of the CDCP set fee.

items.title: Balance billing
items.text: A clinic charge above the plan’s set fee.

items.title: Preauthorization
items.text: A coverage review done before some treatments.

items.title: Frequency limit
items.text: The most times, or how often, a service is covered.
